pharm: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker; inhibits the cardiac pacemaker If (funny) current in the SA node
quick: Start 5 mg BID (2.5 mg BID if vulnerable) with food; max 7.5 mg BID
May cause fetal harm (cardiac teratogenicity); use effective contraception
Mild-moderate: no change; severe (Child-Pugh C): contraindicated
Heart rate, atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, phosphenes
summary: Ivabradine is a hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker that selectively slows the SA-node pacemaker If current to lower heart rate without affecting myocardial contractility. It is indicated to reduce the risk of hospitalization for worsening heart failure in adults with stable, symptomatic chronic heart failure (LVEF <=35%) who are in sinus rhythm with a resting heart rate >=70 bpm and are on maximally tolerated beta-blockers or cannot take them. Key risks include bradycardia and conduction disturbances, atrial fibrillation, fetal toxicity, and luminous phenomena (phosphenes). It is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
indications: To reduce the risk of hospitalization for worsening heart failure in adult patients with stable, symptomatic chronic heart failure with LVEF <=35%, in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate >=70 bpm, who are on maximally tolerated beta-blocker doses or have a contraindication to beta-blocker use

dosage.d: Starting 5 mg twice daily with food; maximum 7.5 mg twice daily
dosage.n: After 2 weeks, adjust to achieve resting heart rate 50 to 60 bpm; then adjust as needed based on heart rate and tolerability

dosage.c: Vulnerable patients / conduction defects or risk of hemodynamic compromise from bradycardia
dosage.d: Starting 2.5 mg twice daily, then increase based on heart rate
Increase dose by 2.5 mg (given twice daily), up to a maximum of 7.5 mg twice daily

dosage.c: Dose adjustment - heart rate 50 to 60 bpm
dosage.n: Target resting heart rate is 50 to 60 bpm

dosage.c: Dose adjustment - heart rate <50 bpm or symptoms of bradycardia
dosage.d: Decrease dose by 2.5 mg (given twice daily); if current dose is 2.5 mg twice daily, discontinue therapy
Oral solution may be used in place of tablets
dosage.n: Tablet is scored and can be divided into 2.5 mg halves

admin: Assess the patient after 2 weeks and adjust dose to reach a resting heart rate of 50 to 60 bpm
Start at 2.5 mg twice daily in patients with conduction defects or where bradycardia could cause hemodynamic compromise
The 5 mg tablet is scored and can be split to give a 2.5 mg dose; oral solution available for those unable to swallow tablets
Regularly monitor cardiac rhythm; discontinue if atrial fibrillation develops
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (contraindicated) and grapefruit juice
moa: Ivabradine blocks the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel responsible for the cardiac pacemaker If current that regulates heart rate. Effects are most pronounced at the SA node; there is no effect on ventricular repolarization or myocardial contractility. Ivabradine can also inhibit the retinal Ih current, which may underlie luminous phenomena (phosphenes).

absolute: Sick sinus syndrome, sinoatrial block, or 3rd-degree AV block, unless a functioning demand pacemaker is present
Pacemaker dependence (heart rate maintained exclusively by the pacemaker)
Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
relative: Sinus node dysfunction or conduction defects (1st/2nd-degree AV block, bundle branch block)
2nd-degree AV block (use not recommended unless a functioning demand pacemaker is present)
Demand pacemaker set to rate >=60 bpm (use not recommended)
monitor: Resting heart rate for bradycardia and conduction disturbances
QT prolongation risk when bradycardia coexists with QT-prolonging drugs

preg: Based on animal findings, ivabradine may cause fetal harm. In pregnant rats, exposures 1 to 3 times the human exposure at the maximum recommended dose caused embryo-fetal toxicity and cardiac teratogenicity (abnormal heart shape, interventricular septal defect, complex anomalies of major arteries) with increased post-natal mortality; rabbits showed increased post-implantation loss. There are no adequate, well-controlled human studies. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception. Heart-rate-dependent pregnant patients with low LVEF should be followed closely for heart-failure destabilization, and third-trimester patients monitored for preterm birth.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with ivabradine.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in patients with renal impairment (creatinine clearance >=15 mL/min). Renal clearance is approximately 4.2 L/h with only about 4% of an oral dose excreted unchanged in urine.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Ivabradine is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), as it has not been studied and increased systemic exposure is anticipated.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., azole antifungals like itraconazole, macrolides like clarithromycin/telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors like nelfinavir, nefazodone) - contraindicated; increase exposure and exacerbate bradycardia/conduction disturbances
Verapamil or diltiazem - increase ivabradine exposure and lower heart rate; avoid
Negative chronotropes (digoxin, amiodarone, beta-blockers) - increased risk of bradycardia; monitor heart rate
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil, grapefruit juice) - avoid concomitant use
CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., St. John's wort, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin) - decrease ivabradine concentrations and efficacy; avoid
QT-prolonging drugs - bradycardia may increase risk of QT prolongation and torsade de pointes
interactions.food: Take with food; food delays absorption. Avoid grapefruit juice (moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor).

serious: Bradycardia, sinus arrest, and heart block
QT prolongation with risk of torsade de pointes (with bradycardia/QT drugs)
emergency: Severe or symptomatic bradycardia, sinus arrest, or heart block

monitoring: Resting heart rate (target 50 to 60 bpm) and symptoms of bradycardia
Cardiac rhythm for new atrial fibrillation - discontinue if it develops
Conduction status, particularly in patients with sinus node dysfunction or AV block
Pregnancy status and use of effective contraception in females of reproductive potential
Visual disturbances (phosphenes), usually in the first 2 months
counsel: Take twice daily with food, as directed
This medicine can harm an unborn baby; use effective birth control and tell your clinician right away if you become pregnant
Do not breastfeed while taking ivabradine
Avoid grapefruit juice and tell your clinician about all medicines, especially antifungals, antibiotics, and heart-rhythm drugs
You may notice brief brightness or halos in your vision (phosphenes), usually early on and often resolving; report if bothersome
Report a slow, fast, or irregular heartbeat, fainting, dizziness, or swelling
Do not stop or change the dose on your own
pk: Dose-dependent heart-rate reduction (~10 bpm at recommended doses), plateau above 20 mg twice daily
Peak plasma concentration about 1 hour under fasting conditions; food delays absorption
Distribution half-life ~2 hours; effective half-life approximately 6 hours
Twice-daily dosing; oral bioavailability ~40% due to first-pass metabolism; CYP3A4 substrate
pearls: Lowers heart rate via SA-node If (funny) current without negative inotropy - useful when beta-blockers are maxed or not tolerated
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated; avoid moderate inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, grapefruit) and CYP3A4 inducers
Only works in sinus rhythm; discontinue if atrial fibrillation develops
Phosphenes (transient visual brightness) arise from retinal Ih inhibition and usually appear within the first 2 months
Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment, acute decompensated HF, significant hypotension/bradycardia, and SA/AV nodal disease without a pacemaker
missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time with food; do not double the dose. Continue twice-daily dosing and do not change the dose without medical advice.
overdose: Overdose may lead to severe and prolonged bradycardia. For bradycardia with poor hemodynamic tolerance, temporary cardiac pacing may be required. Provide supportive treatment, which may include intravenous fluids, atropine, and intravenous beta-stimulating agents such as isoproterenol.
